First public release of ringtrain: distributed training with every byte of communication written by hand.

## Highlights
- Ring all-reduce over framed TCP (reduce-scatter + all-gather, segmented, async sends), pipelined broadcast, dissemination barrier; exact against a naive sum for 1-5 ranks
- DDP-style bucketed gradients with communication/computation overlap; GPipe and 1F1B pipeline schedules, tested against single-process training (1F1B bit-for-bit on a transformer)
- Top-k with error feedback and PowerSGD gradient compression, with a convergence-vs-traffic comparison
- Elastic, fault-tolerant training: checkpoints (model, optimiser, RNG, data cursor) in a raftstore cluster; a worker killed with SIGKILL/TerminateProcess is detected, survivors roll back to the last checkpoint and continue, and a restarted worker re-joins
- dog2real PPO policies train data-parallel through ringtrain (DD-PPO)

## Downloads
- Python wheel and sdist (`pip install ringtrain-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl`; needs numpy and torch)
- `ringtrain-results.tar.gz`: the measured results (JSON, JSONL logs) and figures from the README

## Not yet verified
All measurements so far are worker *processes* on one host over loopback TCP. Still to do on the
real home cluster (NAS, Pi 5, server, M1), with configs in `deploy/`:
- multi-machine scaling over the LAN, with and without compression
- pulling the power on a worker (heartbeat-timeout path) and on a raftstore node
- tinylm through the adapter interface
